thread:
Priya: Quick thread: ran speculative decoding smoke tests on q4_K 70B (pt-quant) with a two-stage fallback draft. TL;DR: ~1.9x median token throughput, small QA EM regression (~0.6pp), but hallucination heuristic increased. Need to sanity-check safety gating before wider rollout.
Alex: Nice. which eval set and exact command did you run?
Priya: Pasted the run below — simple smoke harness we used for onboarding.
Priya: ```
# run spec decode smoke test
python run_spec_decode.py \
  --model ./models/ln70b-q4_K \
  --batch 8 \
  --spec-beam 2 \
  --fallback greedy \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-set eval/smoke_open_qa.jsonl
```
Priya: Key numbers (median across 3 runs): baseline throughput 12.3 toks/s -> spec 23.4 toks/s (1.9x), open_qa EM 72.4 -> 71.8 (-0.6), hallucination_flag_rate 3.1% -> 4.5% (+1.4pp).
Liam: How are you computing hallucination_flag_rate?
Priya: heuristic: answer contains explicit unverifiable claims OR contradicts provided context OR triggers our fact-check regex + cross-check against knowledge-cutoff via external light-checker. It's noisy but directionally useful.
eval-bot: Eval summary (run id 1799854322-1): throughput_median: 23.4; qa_em: 71.8; halluc_rate: 4.5; rouge_l_avg: 0.62
Jen: @Priya can we gate speculative outputs with a reranker/safety check and fallback to greedy for flagged turns? Even if throughput drops, safety-first for prod.
Priya: I tried a naive reranker (logprob + safety_score threshold). Hallucation dropped to 3.6% but throughput fell to ~1.6x. So there's a clear tradeoff.
Alex: Let's run a small human eval on 200 safety-sensitive examples before we change any defaults. Can you upload the eval set and the run config to eng-ml? :thumbsup:
Priya: Done — s3://redwood-evals/spec_smoke/1799854322.jsonl and I pushed configs to the repo under experiments/spec_decoding/smoke_1799854322.yaml. Also tagged quant checkpoint as calib-v2.
Liam: FYI, I saw high variance for long-turn convs; batching + speculative prefetch seems to interact with KV cache eviction. Might explain some hallucination spikes. Filing follow-up.
Priya: Created GH issue redwood/serving#3387 to track kv cache + batching interactions and ablation plan (spec-beam 1 vs 2, batch sizes 4/8/16). I'll run the ablation next week and post results.
Alex: Perfect. thanks Priya. We should avoid enabling spec decode by default for enterprise tenants until human eval and reranker tuning.
Priya: Agreed. I'll coordinate a short playbook for ops: enable flags, rollout %s, and rollback triggers (QA drop >1pp or hallucation +1pp).
Liam: Sounds good.
Jen: Thanks — leaning toward a conservative rollout.
Priya: Closing loop here; will update thread with ablation charts and the human eval spreadsheet when ready.
